subject: Performance SLO: context window & max tokens — latency impact (FinCo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finco.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finco.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO recap & next steps — context window / token limits

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on SLOs and sizing for the pilot: 

Summary of FinCo requirements we discussed:
- 95th percentile latency target: 250ms (interactive flows)
- Typical request: 1.5k input tokens average, 2.5k max; output up to 1k tokens in longer responses
- Peak concurrency observed: ~120 concurrent sessions; target pilot concurrency: 50-80
- Streaming required for the chat UI for partial responses; also need server-side non-stream fallback for batch transforms
- Throughput requirement: ~6 tokens/sec per session (real-time interactive experience)

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) We’ll run guided micro-benchmarks for three representative payloads (short: 200 tokens, medium: 1.5k tokens, long: 3.5k total tokens) - can you confirm the payload distribution and whether the 3.5k is acceptable as the max?
2) I’ve attached a small SLO matrix (perf_slo_matrix.xlsx) with questions on tail latencies by token range - please fill where you can, otherwise we’ll load defaults from our production profiles.
3) Follow-up call: I propose Tue 16 Mar, 10:00-10:30am PT to go over benchmark results and options (streaming vs non-stream streaming optimization tradeoffs).

Notes on context window impact (high level):
- Larger context windows increase KV memory and retrieval time; for autoregressive decoders, per-token latency grows with sequence length in the worst case unless we use aggressive KV cache reuse and optimized kernels.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency for users but doesn’t change total compute - it does, however, often improve UI-level SLOs by delivering partial tokens earlier.
- For 2k+ tokens we typically recommend quantized model variants and batching controls, but this can affect output determinism; we should validate on FinCo prompts.

Attachment: perf_slo_matrix.xlsx (XLSX) - small matrix with token buckets and target percentiles.

Thanks - I’ll loop in Dev to schedule the micro-benchmark.
—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finco.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO recap & next steps — context window / token limits

Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) The 3.5k figure was an upper bound for generated+input in one of our batch workflows; for interactive chat we expect ~2k total tokens max (1.5k in, 500 out). The batch transforms can tolerate higher latency but are also important to price.
2) Streaming is important for customer-facing chat. If streaming requires a model variant or config change that materially increases cost, we need that tradeoff called out.

We’ll fill in what we can in the matrix and send sample payloads by EOD tomorrow.

Can you confirm whether your recommended 95th percentile 250ms applies to the interactive 2k scenario (i.e., end-to-end including network + model time) or just model infer time? Also curious what concurrency headroom we should plan for with reserved capacity (50 vs 80).

On scheduling: Tue 16th 10am PT works for us.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Mercer
Director, AI Platform
FinCo
alex.mercer@finco.com | +1 (617) 555-0899

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@finco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO recap & next steps — context window / token limits

Alex -

Good questions. Quick answers before the call: 

- The 250ms 95th target I mentioned is our UI-level SLO (end-to-end perceived latency) for interactive flows. Model infer time should aim for ~150-180ms 95th to leave room for network, routing, and client processing.

- For 2k total tokens (1.5k in / 500 out) we typically see model infer 95th in the 120-220ms range depending on model family and quantization. If you require streaming (token-by-token), the initial token arrival is usually <100ms, then subsequent tokens stream at a few ms/token depending on batch and kernel efficiency.

- Concurrency: reserved pools sized for 50-80 concurrent interactive sessions is reasonable. For headroom we recommend capacity planning at +25% of expected pilot concurrency (so plan for ~100 if you expect 80). We can provide a cost estimate for reserved capacity vs burstable hosted lanes after the micro-benchmarks.

- Long/batch jobs (3.5k+ tokens) are better handled on a different route with higher latency SLOs - we can route them to dedicated capacity or queue them for batch execution to keep interactive lanes fast.

I’ve attached a short latency reference PDF from our infra team that breaks down model infer time by token buckets and common optimizations (redwood-latency-matrix.pdf).

Next steps for today:
- Dev will run micro-benchmarks on the three payload sizes you approve and share raw numbers.
- Alex / Priya to share sample payload distribution and any example prompts (sensitive data redacted).
- Confirm Tue 16 Mar 10:00 PT call - invite to follow.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: redwood-latency-matrix.pdf (PDF)

Quick note from infra: happy to run the micro-benchmarks - can you confirm the following so we set up an apples-to-apples test?

- Sample prompt examples (we prefer sanitized examples with representative instruction length)
- Tokenization details (are tokens counted pre-BPE or our standard tokenizer? we assume standard BPE used in our models)
- Desired concurrency pattern for the benchmark (steady 50 concurrent sessions vs spike to 80)

Plan: run 3 runs per payload size, report p50/p95/p99 for model infer time, network adj (if you can host a client to measure end-to-end), and config used (batch size, quantization flags, KV caching).

If you share sample prompts to perf@redwood.ai, I’ll queue the runs today and get numbers by EOD Thu.

We’ll sanitize and upload three sample prompt sets to the Drive link you shared (https://drive.google.com/finco/perf-report) by EOD today. Distribution: short 40%, medium 45%, long 15% (longs are usually batch transforms and can be routed differently).

Confirming:
- Interactive target: end-to-end 95th <= 250ms (you’ll aim for model infer ~150ms 95th)
- Streaming required for chat paths; provide cost delta for streaming vs non-stream token-by-token delivery
- Run benchmarks with steady 50 concurrent sessions and one spike run to 80 for headroom numbers

Please go ahead with the runs. We’ll take the Tue 16th slot if you still have it (I know dates shifted - happy to rebook if needed).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

- Alex
